title: Flowise vs n8n (2026): Which Tool Should You Use?
summary: Flowise vs n8n target different parts of AI agent projects. Flowise focuses on agent logic, n8n on workflows, so select based on your challenge.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces for agents that act across business apps


If you want to avoid owning two systems, Activepieces runs its AI agent step inside the same flow that touches your business apps, and it's an open source, MIT-licensed core across 741 integrations.


That removes the host-and-monitor burden of a split stack, but it gives up depth on one side.


### Where it fits the same criteria


Activepieces calls its integrations "pieces," and a connected piece is an agent tool from the moment it exists: the same action runs as a step in a flow and as a tool on the per-project MCP server that Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or your own agent can call.


Nothing is exported or wired twice.


The catalogue is **741 integrations on an MIT-licensed core** , counted from packages/integrations/community in the open source repo, where the action a flow runs is the same one the MCP server exposes as a tool; the Integrations Framework and MCP Server documentation describe both sides.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production, and **roughly 60% of those integrations are community-contributed** , so most teams can likely connect to their essential services without writing custom integrations.


The full list is on the[pieces page](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) , where your CRM, ticketing and finance tools are either listed or not.


The four criteria, applied one at a time:


- For apps the agent can act in, the AI agent step draws on integrations coverage, so it can act wherever an integration exists. Confirm your CRM, ticketing and finance tools are listed. A missing integration means custom work.
- For approval, a flow can pause for a person's decision before a consequential step. Put that pause ahead of any write, refund or send, so the agent proposes and a human commits.
- For self-hosting, the code is open source, so you can run it on your own infrastructure. Regulated data then stays inside your boundary.
- For pricing as runs grow, the $20 Plus plan covers 10,000 runs. Count your expected monthly runs first, because an agent flow with many steps can eat that allowance faster than the trigger count suggests.


Run against the same four criteria, Activepieces comes out as one flow rather than two products joined by a callback: place an Agent step next to a deterministic step, open the run trace, and the whole execution is logged as one run.


The free plan on Activepieces Cloud has unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, with no card needed:[https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fflowise-vs-n8n-2026-which-tool-should-you-use) .


### Where it does not fit


Flowise is the better choice when your hard problem is the agent's reasoning, and Activepieces isn't built for that job. That covers retrieval tuning, multi-agent orchestration and inspecting how the agent reached an answer.


Flowise is Apache 2.0 licensed, and a team that needs that depth gets it there.


n8n's own comparison page credits Flowise with 100+ AI-specific tools and vector databases, so that depth is the reason to choose it.


If you need the widest catalogue of mature app nodes, the same page claims 1,000+ for n8n. That's a vendor's claim, so check it against your own app list. For a large, branching business process, n8n is the stronger default.


Activepieces is the better choice for teams that want their AI agents to act across business apps without owning and monitoring a second system, judged on how little wiring it takes to turn an integration into an agent tool.


Because the same piece action that runs in a flow is the one exposed as a tool on the MCP server, nothing is exported or built twice, and the 741 MIT-licensed integrations are usable by agents from the moment they are connected.


A team that needs more depth on the agent side than a flow-based step provides may weigh that trade-off differently, but for agents that work across CRM, ticketing and finance tools, one system is the simpler one to run.
